results.title: OpenAPI Schemas — Nova Specs documentation
results.content: OpenAPI Schemas — Nova Specs documentation * Sign up for Foundation Membership We would like to start documenting our APIs in an industry-standard, machine-readable manner. The additional schemas will merely validate what is already allowed, which will mean extensive use of Put another way, an API that currently ignores unexpected request body fields or query string parameters will continue to ignore them. This was completed in Dalmatian (2024.2) These will be sourced from existing OpenAPI schemas, currently published at github.com/gtema/openstack-openapi, from Tempest’s API schemas, and where necessary from new schemas auto-generated from JSON response bodies generated in tests and manually modified handle things like enum values. This idea has been rejected because OpenAPI is clearly the best tool for the It is the most widely used API description language available today and aligns well with our existing use of JSON Schema for API validation. Finally, OpenStack’s previous forays into discoverable APIs, such as Keystone’s use of JSONHome or Glance’s attempts to publish resource schemas, have seen limited take-up outside of the projects themselves. Given our existing extensive use of JSON Schema for API validation, it is expected that this should not be a significant issue. ### Developer impact¶ Developers working on the API microversions will now be encouraged to provide JSON Schema schemas for both requests and responses. ### Upgrade impact¶ ### Assignee(s)¶ ### Feature Liaison¶ ### Work Items¶ * Add missing request body schemas * Add tests to validate existence of request body schemas * Add missing query string schemas * Add tests to validate existence of query string schemas * Add decorator to validate response body schemas against response * Add tests to validate existence of response body schemas The actual generation of an OpenAPI documentation will be achieved via a separate tool. Unit, functional and integration tests will all work together to ensure that response body schemas match real responses by setting Initially there should be no impact as we will continue to use `os_api_ref` as-is for our `api-ref` docs. We may wish _not_ to add schemas for these, though by doing so we will lose the ability to generate documentation or clients for these APIs from the OpenAPI spec.

results.title: HAUL (HAWL) | Islamic Relief Singapore
results.content: # HAUL (HAWL) ## **What is Haul (Hawl)?** Hawl is the length of time that an individual must possess the wealth that they will pay Zakat on. ## **What does** **Haul (Hawl)** **mean?** In explanations of Zakat, Hawl means a lunar year and therefore, a haul (lunar year) is approximately 354 days long. ## **If one has not yet possessed his/her wealth for a Haul (lunar year), can s/he still pay Zakat?** Yes s/he can pay Zakat, but they would need to factor in any expenditures or liabilities when calculating how much they would need to pay. ## **My wealth dipped below the Nisab during the course of the year, do I still have to pay Zakat?** Yes, but please discuss with a Scholar. ## **I received a large amount of money just before my Zakat was due for this year. Do I include it in this year’s Zakat?** Yes, you need to include it in your calculation. ## **I have a pension fund, do I pay Zakat on the savings in this fund?** This depends on the nature of the fund. We would suggest you consult a scholar about this as the issue of pension schemes can be quite complex. ## **A group of us have set up a fund to pay for any emergency needs that we may have. Is this liable for Zakat?** It sounds as if the mentioned fund would count as a Waqf. The general rule is that a Waqf is not liable for Zakat. As long as, there is no personal ownership, or nobody is personally benefitting from this fund, and also depending on the nature of the fund, Zakat may/may not be liable. However, you would need to check this with a scholar. ### **Zakat** **Resources** * Pay Zakat ul Fitr (Fitrana) © Copyright 2025 Islamic Relief Worldwide, Inc. All rights reserved. ## QUICK DONATE

results.title: OpenAPI: Guide for API Development and Collaboration
results.content: **OpenAPI** is a widely adopted standard that allows developers to describe and document APIs in a machine-readable format. **OpenAPI** is an industry-standard specification for defining and documenting RESTful APIs. It allows developers to describe their API's structure, operations, request parameters, responses, and security mechanisms in a standardized, machine-readable format. ## **Why OpenAPI is Essential for API Development**. At its core, OpenAPI allows developers to define **schemas** for API requests and responses. These tools parse the OpenAPI document and create user-friendly, interactive interfaces where developers can explore the API, see available endpoints, and even make test requests. Tasks like API documentation generation, testing, and mocking can be automated using OpenAPI, saving developers time and reducing manual work. With tools like **Postman** that support OpenAPI, developers can quickly generate mock servers, test cases, and documentation, speeding up the entire API development lifecycle. OpenAPI enables the automatic generation of **interactive API documentation**, which helps developers understand how to use the API, explore available endpoints, and test them directly from the documentation. Using OpenAPI, developers can automate testing processes to ensure that APIs behave as expected. Tools like Postman and Swagger Validator can be used to validate API responses against the defined schemas in the OpenAPI document. Postman has integrated support for **OpenAPI tags**, which allows developers to organize their API collections based on the tags defined in the OpenAPI document. OpenAPI allows developers to define the structure of API requests and responses. Use validation tools like **Postman** to test your API requests and responses against the OpenAPI document. Tools like **Postman**have integrated OpenAPI to further enhance workflows, making it easier than ever to create high-quality, well-documented APIs. As the demand for APIs continues to grow, OpenAPI will remain a key component of the API development lifecycle. 3. results.title: Nisab of Zakat 2025: Meaning, Timing, and Calculation
results.content: What Is The Nisab Of Zakat. # How Much is Zakat Nisab in 2025? Let’s explore what the nisab of zakat is, its current value, its importance, when it is due, and its calculations. ## What is the Nisab of Zakat in Islam? Nisab is the minimum wealth a Muslim must possess before Zakat becomes obligatory. * **Gold Zakat Nisab:** 3 ounces (87.48 grams). * **Silver Zakat Nisab:** 21 ounces (612.36 grams). Zakat is calculated at **2.5% of total wealth**, provided it meets or exceeds the Nisab threshold. ## Zakat Nisab as of January 2025. Here are the current Zakat Nisab thresholds based on the values of silver and gold:. ## Nisab and Zakat Rate for Different Types of Assets. ## When is Zakat Nisab Due? Zakat becomes obligatory on assets such as gold, cash, and property when they exceed the Nisab threshold within the Hijri year, a lunar calendar cycle. 1. **Maliki, Shafi‘i, and Hanbali Schools**: If wealth falls below the Nisab threshold within the lunar year, the Zakat year restarts. 2. **Hanafi School**: If wealth drops below the Nisab after initially reaching it, the Zakat schedule doesn't change, as long as the wealth meets the Nisab at the beginning of the Zakat year (hawl) and on the due date. “A” marks when other legal schools restart the Zakat year because wealth dropped below, then rose back to, the Nisab threshold. ## Nisab and Zakat Calculation for Personal and Business Wealth. The Nisab for different types of Zakatable wealth is determined in monetary terms. ## Importance of Zakat Nisab in Islam. Zakat nisab on different assets ensures that your wealth is calculated accurately and that you pay the right amount of Zakat. Timing is key, as Zakat is due once your wealth reaches the nisab threshold, and it must be calculated annually. By calculating Zakat on personal and business wealth under the Nisab, individuals uphold the principles of charity and social responsibility. ### Should I use silver or gold when using the Nisab for calculating Zakat? ### How do you calculate Zakat Nisab on cash? If your cash assets exceed the nisab threshold, you are obligated to pay Zakat on them.

results.title: API Handyman | We need specialized tools for API design reviews
results.content: 1 - 3 good reasons to do API Design Reviews 2 - An API design review is based on facts, not opinions 3 - We need specialized tools for API design reviews. # We need specialized tools for API design reviews. Doing an API design review is not only about that, but it will require, sooner or later, to analyze an interface contract. But, after dozens of reviews, you may realize that, despite using the “right” existing tools, the API space actually lacks API design reviews specialized tools. # ~~Reviewing API designs~~ Helping people. I’ve seen people making API design reviews by directly reading OpenAPI files such as the one below. I don’t know how you feel, but reading this raw OpenAPI file do not really help me to make a complete review of the design. That’s interesting, but when I do an API design review my first move is trying to guess what the API is made for by looking at all of its operations, all GET /this and POST /that and their summaries. As far as I remember, I always took advantage of documentation tools to do API design reviews. I don’t use it only because it was the only one available when I started being an API design reviewer and I don’t want to change my habits. [apihandyman.io] $ Spectral lint -r OpenAPI 3.x detected 358:26 warning property-name-no-number Property name must not contain number (maybe you can use an array) #/components/schemas/Episode_Single/properties/alternate_name_1 360:26 warning property-name-no-number Property name must not contain number (maybe you can use an array) #/components/schemas/Episode_Single/properties/alternate_name_2 ✖ 2 problems (0 errors, 2 warnings, 0 infos, 0 hints). As you can see linting an OpenAPI file is not only about doing dumb checks (even if only just that actually changed my life), you can use Spectral to spot possible design patterns and business domain concerns. I hope that what was shown here will give you some ideas about how analyze OpenAPI files but more important, I hope you’ll understand that we, API designer reviewers, need specialized tools to do our job. We need tools that take advantage of this machine readable format, tools such as Spectral, but we need new way of rendering OpenAPI files and linter results.
